paragraphs: A substation breaker is three tall porcelain or composite columns standing on a steel frame, with the interrupting mechanism at the top of each and the operating linkage below. The height is insulation: at these voltages the distance through air is what keeps the current where it belongs.
The mesh runs 75,342 polygons and 80,385 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the insulator sheds, the terminals and the operating mechanism housing.

At $24 and built to StemCell specification, it suits electrical grid and utility visualisation, energy infrastructure presentation, substation and industrial scenes, engineering material and games. On sale since 2025.

A hand cranked pasta machine is a set of rollers in a chromed frame, with a clamp that grips a table edge, a thickness dial on the side and a crank that fits into one of two positions. That clamp is what makes it a kitchen tool rather than an appliance - it has no motor and no power lead at all.
The mesh is efficient at 25,320 polygons and 25,515 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the rollers, the dial and the clamp.

A silver version sits on this page at the same $24. Both suit kitchen and culinary visualisation, cookware retail renders, recipe and food editorial imagery, restaurant interiors and games. On sale since 2022.

A pop-up play tunnel is a fabric tube over a sprung wire hoop frame, which is why it holds a circular section without any rigid structure and why it twists flat into a disc for storage. The fabric sags slightly between hoops, and that sag is what makes it read as soft rather than as a pipe.
The mesh is minimal at 6,862 polygons and 6,888 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a smooth fabric tube where the interest is in the drape.
At $24 it suits children's play and nursery visualisation, family and lifestyle imagery, toy retail renders, playroom and garden scenes, and games. On sale since 2022.

Socks modelled on a foot are far more useful than socks lying flat. The fabric stretches over the heel, ribs at the cuff, creases at the ankle and takes the shape of the toes - none of which happens to a flat garment, and all of which is what makes hosiery look worn rather than folded.
The mesh is light at 13,872 polygons and 13,876 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the ribbing and the heel and toe shaping.

This page carries a blue version at $24 and two further builds at $29. All suit apparel and sportswear retail renders, e-commerce imagery, character set dressing for film, television and games, and lifestyle advertising. On sale since 2022.

Longan grows in hanging bunches on woody stems, and that arrangement is the identification: the fruit is never sold or seen singly, always as a cluster still attached to the branch. The skin is thin, tan and slightly rough, quite unlike the spiky relative it is usually compared to.
The mesh runs 75,083 polygons and 75,490 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the individual fruits and the stem structure holding them.
At $24 it suits food and produce visualisation, tropical and Asian cuisine imagery, grocery and market scenes, packaging and menu material, and games. On sale since 2024.

A low polygon figure is a stylistic choice rather than a limitation. Faceted forms, no facial detail and flat colour give a look that reads clearly at small size and in motion, which is why the style dominates explainer animation, mobile games and infographics where realism would be a distraction.
The mesh is deliberately tiny at 1,632 polygons and 1,607 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is what lets a crowd of these figures fill a scene at no cost.

Three rigged builds share this page at $39, including versions prepared for Cinema 4D and for Maya. Aimed at explainer and motion graphics, mobile games, infographic and corporate illustration, and interface work. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2024.

A stylised soldier reads by silhouette alone: helmet, webbing, boots and a rifle held across the body. At this polygon count there is no room for detail, so the pose and the outline carry all of the identification - which is exactly the discipline that makes low polygon design work.
The mesh is minimal at 1,856 polygons and 1,848 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, light enough that an entire formation costs almost nothing to render.

Three rigged builds share this page at $39, including versions prepared for Cinema 4D and for Maya. Aimed at strategy and mobile games, explainer and infographic animation, military visualisation at scale, and illustration. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2024.

River pebbles are rounded by water rather than broken by machinery, which gives them smooth flattened shapes with no sharp edges and a very narrow size range within any one bed. That uniformity is what distinguishes river gravel from crushed aggregate at a glance.

This is a scatter asset rather than a single object: the geometry is deliberately minimal so that thousands of instances can cover a bed, a border or a planter without any render cost. Mixed UV layout lets the stones take varied surface treatment across a scatter.

At $24 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits landscape and garden visualisation, architectural exteriors, aquarium and interior decor, riverbank and terrain scenes, and games. On sale since 2026.

A temporary works sign is a diamond plate on a folding trestle rather than a fixed post, because it has to be put out in the morning and taken in at night. Orange rather than yellow marks it as temporary, and the frame legs are weighted or sandbagged so wind from passing traffic does not take it.

The mesh is efficient at 28,516 polygons and 14,894 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the plate face as its own surface so a different legend can be applied without remodelling.
At $24 it suits roadworks and highway visualisation, traffic management presentation, driving simulators and games, urban and street set dressing, and safety material. On sale since 2023.

A small softener bottle is built around its cap: the cap doubles as the measuring cup, so it is oversized relative to the neck and shaped to hold a dose. The handle is moulded into the body rather than added, and the whole thing is designed to pour without glugging.
The mesh is minimal at 1,177 polygons and 1,186 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a smooth moulded bottle whose detail comes from the label.
At $24 it suits household product packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, supermarket and e-commerce renders, laundry and utility interiors, and games. On sale since 2022.

A cut glass decanter is a refraction problem before it is a shape problem. The facets cut into the body split the light into dozens of internal reflections, and the heavy ornate stopper adds another set. Modelled smooth the object reads as a plain bottle; the cutting is the entire character.
The mesh is minimal at 1,324 polygons and 1,318 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits glassware where the material and the faceting carry the realism rather than density.

At $24 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits interior and hospitality visualisation, spirits and luxury advertising, bar and dining set dressing, antique and period interiors, and games. On sale since 2025.

The egg shaped virtual pet is a small dot matrix screen surrounded by a shell, with three buttons below it and a key ring at the top. Everything about it is designed for a pocket and for a child's hand, and the three buttons are the entire interface - which is why the design has barely changed in decades.
The mesh is light at 11,414 polygons and 5,726 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the screen as a separate surface so a display image can be applied without masking.
At $24 it suits retro technology and nostalgia visualisation, toy retail and merchandise renders, nineties period interiors, product advertising and games. On sale since 2023.

The record itself is an ordinary phonograph disc, but the cover is not: it carries an engraved diagram explaining how to play the record, where the spacecraft came from and what the two hydrogen states are, all in symbols meant to be readable by someone with no shared language at all.
The mesh is light at 5,504 polygons and 2,754 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the disc, the cover plate and the engraved relief.

At $24 and built to StemCell specification, it suits space and science communication, museum and exhibition material, documentary and education content, editorial illustration, print and games. On sale since 2024.

A water cooler bottle is a moulded jug with a deep grip ring at the neck, ribbed sides for stiffness and a wide flat top that sits inverted on a dispenser. It is designed to be carried by one person, tipped and dropped into place, and every feature on it serves that awkward handling.
The mesh is 9,108 polygons and 9,116 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the blue tint and the moulded lettering.
At $19 it suits office and workplace interior visualisation, water dispenser and beverage marketing, warehouse and storage scenes, retail renders and games. On sale since 2020.
